sections.title: Canonical goal backend
sections.rationale: replace with capability evidence and repository identity
sections.instructions: Use the CLI-selected backend as the authority for shared goal state. Require the repository identity and observed capability evidence to match; never fall back silently.

sections.title: Git, review, and release
sections.rationale: uses provider-native stack context when proven while preserving independently reviewable PR gates and a named compatible fallback
sections.instructions: Follow repository rules and the CLI-selected pull-request mode. Keep one branch and pull request per source-changing goal and one active stack. Base dependent work on the exact reviewed dependency checkpoint, make verified sub-goal commits, collect human pull-request approval at true queue exhaustion, and integrate in dependency order. Never bypass policy review, required checks, merge authority, or release authority. Preserve or migrate shipped contracts. Only evidenced unreleased contracts may permit bounded replacement of affected project-owned state within existing authority; ambiguous evidence blocks that action. Releases refresh affected contract evidence, not unchanged policy approval.

sections.title: Verification and testing
sections.rationale: prevents unobservable product changes and false confidence without manufacturing documentation or test meta-tests
sections.instructions: Require artifact-appropriate observable evidence in small chunks. Documentation and test cases need no recursive tests; product behavior and reusable test infrastructure require direct verification. Use the smallest unique falsifiable local probe, widen when relevant, inspect exact pull-request-head CI when configured, and capture test-discovered product bugs separately.

sections.title: Code-quality and refactoring boundaries
sections.instructions: Preserve behavior unless a goal explicitly authorizes a behavior change. Without a feature goal, limit cleanup to behavior-preserving changes; remove dead code only with evidence and treat dynamic, generated, and vendored code conservatively.

sections.title: Dependencies, tooling, and generated artifacts
sections.rationale: replace with repository-specific commands and ownership evidence
sections.instructions: Use project-native tooling, do not hand-edit generated artifacts, and make dependency changes only with explicit goal scope and verification.

sections.title: Security, privacy, secrets, and compliance
sections.rationale: record applicable project constraints without making safety optional
sections.instructions: Never expose secrets or mutate production without authority. Repository rules may tighten but cannot weaken safety, privacy, or compliance boundaries.

sections.title: Documentation and style
sections.rationale: keep communication project-appropriate while providing a concise ZzzOps fallback
sections.default_origin: ZzzOps fallback overridden by repository or user evidence
sections.instructions: Follow evidenced repository documentation and style conventions, communicate outcomes first, and include implementation detail only where it helps decisions.

sections.title: Deployment, environment, and resources
sections.rationale: limits external impact and avoids multiplying large writable checkouts
sections.instructions: Do not deploy without authority. Prefer bounded worktree parallelism below the reviewed 100 MiB tracked-worktree threshold and read-only investigation at or above it; wait rather than duplicate active delegated work.

sections.title: Engineering rigor
sections.rationale: Balance production-oriented specification and verification with escalation-ready harness investment; higher-risk work can automatically require agentic evidence.
sections.instructions: Assess engineering risk and commitment carefully, raise rigor when evidence warrants it, and scale requirements discovery from light through thorough with effective rigor.

sections.title: Model routing and delegation
sections.rationale: Select the least expensive available model that satisfies the phase capability floor while keeping root-level and above-root authority explicit.
sections.instructions: Route each phase by effective rigor, consequence, boundedness, and phase type. Refresh runtime model and effort availability, select only reviewed pairs at sufficient capability and least cost, keep human interaction on root, allow workers above root capability only when reviewed policy enables allow_above_root_delegation, and persist a blocker when no reviewed capable pair is available.

sections.title: ZzzOps workflow adherence
sections.rationale: Require durable goal context for substantial agent work while allowing projects to review stricter or lighter routing.
sections.instructions: Require durable tracked goals for substantial repository work. Read-only investigation and ZzzOps administration are exempt; only explicit scoped user authority grants an exception. Execute the one strict adaptable declarative evidence DAG. Root owns stable human questions, approvals, publication and merge; independent delegated agents investigate and review configured risks. Preserve unaffected Results through correction, require reviewed atomic non-applicability to retain the leaf path, and consume child delivery Results read-only for composition.

nodes.prompt: Root consolidates the immutable goal request and admitted questions/findings into stable question identities. Preserve the same id, source, blocking decision, status, answer, revision and provenance across revisions; do not repeat or re-ask a settled question unless its exact source or an admitted applicable finding changes. Root alone asks the human. Every revised Result consumes the retained admitted correction through host obligation currentness. Declare investigation items for technical unknowns.

Synthesize the exact requirements and every joined applicable investigation Result into a falsifiable specification. Preserve answers, constraints, assumptions, risks and criteria. Declare acceptance_contracts and maintainability_entropy review members plus every evidence-backed applicable domain risk; non-applicability needs evidence. Emit a finite workspace allocation for test_design, implement, and parent integration work; it grants no edit authority.

Root reviews the exact specification, requirements, investigation Results and every independent spec review member Result. Every member decision must be approved by content, not merely present. Approve only when all typed findings and human questions are resolved or justified non-applicable; issue workspace authorization for the exact specification allocation and decomposition proposition.

Derive finite independently deliverable goals or work items from the approved specification. Choose leaf or composition. Atomic is reviewed decomposition non-applicability, not a delivery topology or shortcut: prove one indivisible workspace responsibility, no independently deliverable child boundary, and no useful parallel ownership; retain the complete leaf path.

Independently review exact specification, approval, workspace allocation and decomposition for coherent boundaries, dependencies and absence of ownership cycles. Reject unjustified atomic non-applicability; atomic must prove indivisible responsibility, no independently deliverable boundary and no useful parallel ownership while retaining every leaf delivery phase. Authorize only exact reviewed allocation tasks.
In the authorized leaf or atomic-parent workspace, implement meaningful tests/evidence for every falsifiable criterion and known risk.

sections.title: Automated design authority
sections.rationale: Allow unattended execution to resolve low-commitment in-scope design choices when reviewed project evidence is decisive, escalate high-commitment choices through early evidence, and retain hard authority gates.
sections.instructions: Automated design is disabled by default. If an explicit reviewed policy enables it, limit it to bounded in-scope implementation: compare alternatives and structural cost for high-commitment choices, record assumptions and a falsifiable signal, prefer unambiguously risk-reducing privacy or security changes, and block on product scope, incompatible contracts, destructive migration, spending, deployment, external writes, human review, safety authority, or higher authority.

sections.title: Autonomy, approvals, and parallelism
sections.rationale: keeps active capture, reporting, resource, concurrency, and refill choices while phase policy owns execution and approval behavior
sections.instructions: Capture requirements adaptively with the requesting user; during unattended execution persist consequential questions as blockers. Keep human interaction on root, enforce reviewed worker and resource limits, record privacy-safe execution diagnostics, and suggest only bounded valuable work in reviewed categories. Keep worktrees clean, remove or deliberately reuse them after work, and never abandon dirty worktrees. Do not automatically adopt suggested defaults without review.
